5
6	# routers/web — the HTML route table and page handlers
7
8	**Read when:** adding or changing a page, a form POST, or a guard on a web route.
9	**Not here:** the `ctx` value itself -> `services-context.md`; form structs -> `services-forms-and-convert.md`; JSON endpoints -> `routers-api-v1.md`.
10
11	## Responsibilities
12
13	- `routers/web/web.go` — `Routes` assembles the middleware chain; `registerWebRoutes` declares
14	  every HTML route in nested `m.Group` blocks.
15	- `routers/web/{repo,user,org,admin,auth,explore,feed,events,misc,healthcheck,devtest,shared}/` —
16	  the handlers themselves. `events` is the server-sent-events endpoint; `devtest` is the
17	  `/devtest` component gallery.
18	- `routers/common/` — middleware and helpers shared with the API layer.
19	- `modules/web/` — a thin chi wrapper: `NewRouter`, `BeforeRouting`, `AfterRouting`, `Mount`,
20	  `Bind`, `GetForm`.
21
22	## Key files
23
24	| Path | What it holds |
25	| --- | --- |
26	| `routers/web/web.go` | `Routes`, `registerWebRoutes`, `verifyAuthWithOptions` |
27	| `routers/web/repo/issue.go` | a representative handler set, and the `templates.TplName` constants |
28	| `routers/common/pagetmpl.go` | `PageGlobalData` — data every template can rely on |
29	| `routers/common/middleware.go` | `MustInitSessioner` |
30	| `routers/common/blockexpensive.go`, `qos.go` | `BlockExpensive`, `QoS` load shedding |
31	| `routers/common/errpage.go` | the panic/error page renderer |
32	| `modules/web/router.go` | `Bind`, `GetForm` |
33	| `services/context/context_response.go` | `HTML`, and the dev-only `ctx.Data["TemplateName"]` |
34	| `templates/base/footer_content.tmpl` | prints that template name in the page footer |
35
36	## Conventions & invariants
37
38	- A handler is `func Foo(ctx *context.Context)` from `gitea.dev/services/context`. It puts data in
39	  `ctx.Data`, then calls `ctx.HTML(http.StatusOK, tplFoo)`.
40	- `tplFoo` is a package-level `templates.TplName` constant whose value is a path under `templates/`
41	  without the extension — `tplIssues templates.TplName = "repo/issue/list"`.
42	- `ctx.Data` is the only channel from handler to template. A template cannot reach anything the
43	  handler did not put there.
44	- Sign-in guards are local variables built at the top of `registerWebRoutes` from
45	  `verifyAuthWithOptions`: `reqSignIn`, `reqSignOut`, `optSignIn`, `optExploreSignIn`. A new guard
46	  is declared there too, not in a subpackage.
47	- Repo pages get `context.RepoAssignment` (see `services-context.md`), which fills `ctx.Repo`;
48	  ref-scoped pages add `context.RepoRefByType`.
49	- A POST that takes a form is registered as
50	  `m.Post("/path", web.Bind(forms.XxxForm{}), handler)`; the handler reads it back with
51	  `web.GetForm(ctx)`.
52	- The middleware chain in `Routes` is, in order: `chi_middleware.GetHead`, optional gzip,
53	  `common.MustInitSessioner`, `context.Contexter`, the web auth middleware, `goGet`,
54	  `common.PageGlobalData`, then `common.BlockExpensive` and `common.QoS`.
55
56	## Recipes
57
58	**Add a page.**
59
60	1. Handler in the matching `routers/web/<area>/` file, signature `func(ctx *context.Context)`.
61	2. A `templates.TplName` constant beside the other constants in that file.
62	3. The template file at the matching path under `templates/`.
63	4. The route inside the right `m.Group` in `registerWebRoutes`, with the guards that group needs.
64	5. Any user-visible string as a key in `options/locale/locale_en-US.json` — never a literal.
65
66	**Add a form POST.** Do the above, plus a form struct in `services/forms/` and `web.Bind` on the
67	route. See `services-forms-and-convert.md`.
68
69	**Find the template behind a page you are looking at.** Outside production, `ctx.HTML` sets
70	`ctx.Data["TemplateName"]` and `templates/base/footer_content.tmpl` prints it in the page footer, so
71	a dev instance names its own template on every page. Failing that, grep the visible string in
72	`options/locale/locale_en-US.json` for its key, then grep that key under `templates/`. To go the
73	other way, from a template to its handler, grep for the `TplName` value — the template path without
74	the extension.
75
76	## Gotchas
77
78	- The static routes registered on `routes` *before* the `mid` slice is assembled (`/assets/*`,
79	  `/avatars/*`, `/favicon.ico`, `/api/healthz`) deliberately bypass session and auth middleware.
80	  Do not add an authenticated route there.
81	- `registerWebRoutes` is long. Find your group by URL prefix rather than reading top to bottom, and
82	  add the route to the group that already carries the guards you need instead of re-listing them.
83	- `ctx.HTML` after something has already written the response is a bug; `ctx.Written()` reports
84	  whether that happened.
85
86	## Related
87
88	- `services-context.md` — what `ctx` carries and the response helpers
89	- `routers-api-v1.md` — the JSON side of the same handlers
90	- `architecture.md` — where routing sits in the dependency direction
91
```
</details></tool-use>

			pos1++

			s = s[:pos1] + s[pos2:]

```text
1	---

3	verified-at: c0092050a4
4	---
5
6	# architecture — layers, dependency direction, request lifecycle
7
8	**Read when:** you are unsure which layer a change belongs in, which package to import, or how a
9	request reaches your handler.
10	**Not here:** per-package detail -> the doc for that path in `INDEX.md`; test tiers -> `testing.md`.
11
12	## Responsibilities
13
14	| Layer | Owns |
15	| --- | --- |
16	| `cmd/` | CLI subcommands (`web`, `serv`, `hook`, `doctor`, `admin *`) |
17	| `routers/` | HTTP handlers, split into `web`, `api`, `private`, `install`, plus shared `common` |
18	| `services/` | business logic tying routers to models; also the request context and form binding |
19	| `models/` | XORM beans and database queries; keeps external dependencies to a minimum |
20	| `modules/` | standalone leaf utilities with few dependencies |
21	| `templates/` | Go `html/template` sources for server-rendered pages and mail |
22	| `web_src/` | frontend sources (TypeScript, Vue, CSS), built by vite into `public/assets/` |
23	| `options/` | shipped data: locales, gitignores, licenses, labels, readmes |
24
25	## Key files
26
27	| Path | What it holds |
28	| --- | --- |
29	| `main.go` | binary entry point; wires the `cmd` subcommands |
30	| `routers/init.go` | `NormalRoutes` — mounts `/`, `/api/v1`, `/api/internal`, `/api/packages`, `/api/actions` |
31	| `routers/web/web.go` | `Routes` (middleware chain) and `registerWebRoutes` (the whole web route table) |
32	| `routers/api/v1/api.go` | `Routes` plus every API guard middleware |
33	| `services/context/context.go` | `Context`, the value every web handler receives |
34	| `modules/reqctx/datastore.go` | request-scoped key/value store underneath the context |
35	| `docs/guidelines-backend.md` | authoritative backend rules; this doc only summarises them |
36	| `docs/guidelines-refactoring.md` | process rules for when a refactor needs its own PR |
37
38	## Conventions & invariants
39
40	Dependencies flow one way only (`docs/guidelines-backend.md`):
41
42	```text
43	cmd → routers → services → models → modules
44	```
45
46	A package on the left may import a package on its right, but never the reverse. A backwards import
47	is the most common structural review rejection — move the code rather than adding the import.
48
49	- Top-level packages are plural (`services`, `models`, `routers`); subpackages are singular
50	  (`services/user`, `models/repo`).
51	- Cross-layer name collisions take a snake_case import alias: `issues_model`, `user_service`,
52	  `access_model`, and `api "gitea.dev/modules/structs"`. Match the aliases already used in the file
53	  you are editing.
54	- The module path in this fork is `gitea.dev`, **not** `code.gitea.io/gitea`. Copy import paths
55	  from a neighbouring file, not from upstream docs or search results.
56	- There is no `modules/context` in this tree. The request context lives in `services/context`
57	  because it has to depend on models and services.
58	- A function that participates in a transaction takes `context.Context` as its first parameter, so
59	  the transaction propagates. Never pass a `*xorm.Session` as a parameter.
60
61	## Recipes
62
63	**Decide where new code goes.** Does it read or write the database? `models/`. Does it coordinate
64	several model calls, or fan out to mail / notifications / webhooks? `services/`. Does it read the
65	request or write the response? `routers/`. Is it a pure helper with no Gitea dependencies?
66	`modules/`.
67
68	**Trace a web request.** `routers/init.go` (`NormalRoutes`) → `routers/web/web.go` (`Routes` builds
69	the middleware chain; `registerWebRoutes` matches the path) → a handler in
70	`routers/web/{repo,user,org,admin,auth,explore}/` with signature `func(ctx *context.Context)` →
71	services → models → the handler fills `ctx.Data[...]` and calls `ctx.HTML(http.StatusOK, tplFoo)`,
72	where `tplFoo` is a package-level `templates.TplName` naming a file under `templates/`.
73
74	**Trace an API request.** The same until `routers/api/v1/api.go`, then a handler
75	`func(ctx *context.APIContext)` that converts models to a `modules/structs` type and returns it
76	with `ctx.JSON`.
77
78	## Gotchas
79
80	- Run `make fmt` before committing, `make lint-go` / `make lint-js` before pushing, and `make tidy`
81	  after any `go.mod` change (`AGENTS.md`). `make help` lists every target.
82	- Changing a struct under `models/` that is persisted to the database almost always requires a new
83	  migration in `models/migrations/`.
84	- `templates/` and `web_src/` sit outside the dependency rule, but a template may only use data the
85	  handler actually put in `ctx.Data`.
86	- `docs/guidelines-refactoring.md` limits refactor scope: fix the root cause, keep the PR tight,
87	  and split large refactors across PRs.
88
89	## Related
90
91	- `testing.md` — which test tier to write and how to set it up
92	- `docs/guidelines-backend.md`, `docs/guidelines-frontend.md` — the authoritative rules
93
```
</details></tool-use>

// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT

package templates

import (
	"context"
	"html/template"
	"mime"
	"path/filepath"
	"strconv"
	"strings"
	"time"

	activities_model "gitea.dev/models/activities"
	repo_model "gitea.dev/models/repo"
	user_model "gitea.dev/models/user"
	"gitea.dev/modules/gitrepo"
	"gitea.dev/modules/json"
	"gitea.dev/modules/log"
	"gitea.dev/modules/repository"
	"gitea.dev/modules/setting"
	"gitea.dev/modules/svg"

	"github.com/editorconfig/editorconfig-core-go/v2"
)

func sortArrow(normSort, revSort, urlSort string, isDefault bool) template.HTML {
	// if needed
	if len(normSort) == 0 || len(urlSort) == 0 {
		return ""
	}

	if len(urlSort) == 0 && isDefault {
		// if sort is sorted as default add arrow tho this table header
		if isDefault {
			return svg.RenderHTML("octicon-triangle-down", 16)
		}
	} else {
		// if sort arg is in url test if it correlates with column header sort arguments
		// the direction of the arrow should indicate the "current sort order", up means ASC(normal), down means DESC(rev)
		switch urlSort {
		case normSort:
			// the table is sorted with this header normal
			return svg.RenderHTML("octicon-triangle-up", 16)
		case revSort:
			// the table is sorted with this header reverse
			return svg.RenderHTML("octicon-triangle-down", 16)
		}
	}
	// the table is NOT sorted with this header
	return ""
}

// Actioner describes an action
type Actioner interface {
	GetOpType() activities_model.ActionType
	GetActUserName(ctx context.Context) string
	GetRepoUserName(ctx context.Context) string
	GetRepoName(ctx context.Context) string

package templates

import (
	"html/template"
	"io"
	"strings"
	"testing"

	"github.com/stretchr/testify/assert"
)

func TestDict(t *testing.T) {
	type M map[string]any
	cases := []struct {
		args []any
		want map[string]any
	}{
		{[]any{"a", 1, "b", 2}, M{"a": 1, "b": 2}},
		{[]any{".", M{"base": 1}, "b", 2}, M{"base": 1, "b": 2}},
		{[]any{"a", 1, ".", M{"extra": 2}}, M{"a": 1, "extra": 2}},
		{[]any{"a", 1, ".", map[string]int{"int": 2}}, M{"a": 1, "int": 2}},
		{[]any{".", nil, "b", 2}, M{"b": 2}},

1	---
2	scope: Makefile, package.json, pyproject.toml, vite.config.ts, .golangci.yml, eslint.config.ts, stylelint.config.ts

4	---
5
6	# build and tooling — targets, linters, generated files
7
8	**Read when:** a lint or build step fails, or you are unsure which command to run before pushing.
9	**Not here:** the test tiers -> `testing.md`; first-time setup -> `STUDENTS.md`.
10
11	## Responsibilities
12
13	The `Makefile` is the entry point for everything. `make help` lists every target; the ones below
14	are the ones a course task actually needs.
15
16	## Key files
17
18	| Path | What it holds |
19	| --- | --- |
20	| `Makefile` | every build, lint, test and generate target |
21	| `package.json`, `pnpm-lock.yaml` | frontend dependencies |
22	| `vite.config.ts` | the frontend build |
23	| `.golangci.yml` | Go linter configuration |
24	| `eslint.config.ts`, `stylelint.config.ts` | JS/TS and CSS linting |
25	| `.editorconfig` | whitespace rules enforced by `make lint-editorconfig` |
26	| `pyproject.toml`, `uv.lock` | the Python tools behind `make lint-templates`: `djlint`, `yamllint`, `zizmor` |
27	| `tools/lint-shell.sh` | shellcheck, run over `git ls-files '*.sh'` |
28	| `tools/lint-go-all.go` | `lintGoHeader` — the copyright-header check, plus the golangci-lint passes |
29
30	## Conventions & invariants
31
32	- **Before committing:** `make fmt`. **Before pushing:** `make lint-go` for Go changes,
33	  `make lint-js` for TypeScript (`AGENTS.md`), `make lint-templates` for `.tmpl` changes.
34	- `make fmt` covers Go **and** templates, and rewrites the whole repository rather than your diff.
35	- **After any `go.mod` change:** `make tidy`, and justify the dependency change in the PR
36	  description (`docs/guidelines-backend.md`).
37	- New `.go` files need a copyright header with the current year (`AGENTS.md`). `lintGoHeader` in
38	  `tools/lint-go-all.go` enforces the exact `// Copyright <year> The Gitea Authors...` +
39	  `// SPDX-License-Identifier:` form.
40	- `.golangci.yml` `depguard` **bans imports**: `encoding/json` (use `modules/json`), `io/ioutil`,
41	  `golang.org/x/exp`, `gopkg.in/ini.v1` (use the config system), and `modules/git/internal`.
42	- `gci` enforces import order: standard library, then `prefix(gitea.dev)`, then a blank line, then
43	  everything else. `gofumpt` with `extra-rules` formats on top of `gofmt`. `make fmt` applies both.
44	- `CONTRIBUTING.md` requires **"after" screenshots on any PR that changes the UI**, and "before"
45	  screenshots too unless it is a new feature.
46	- No trailing whitespace, LF endings, final newline — `.editorconfig`, checked by
47	  `make lint-editorconfig`.
48	- **Generated files are committed and verified in CI.** `templates/swagger/v1_json.tmpl` comes from
49	  `make generate-swagger`, and `make swagger-check` fails when it is stale
50	  (`routers-api-v1.md`). Never hand-edit a generated file.
51	- `make lint-md` only checks root-level `*.md`. `make lint-shell` shellchecks every tracked `.sh`,
52	  which includes `.claude-students/check.sh`.
53	- Conventional Commits for commit messages and PR titles; add an
54	  `Assisted-by: AGENT_NAME:MODEL_VERSION` trailer; never add `Co-Authored-By` or `Signed-off-by`
55	  (`AGENTS.md`).
56
57	## Recipes
58
59	**Build and run.** `make build` then `./gitea web`. `make watch` rebuilds on change during
60	development.
61
62	**The targets worth memorising.**
63
64	```sh
65	make fmt            # format Go and templates
66	make lint-go        # Go linters
67	make lint-js        # TypeScript linters
68	make lint-templates # djlint over templates/ — needs uv
69	make lint-editorconfig  # whitespace and final newlines, any file type
70	make tidy           # after go.mod changes
71	make generate-swagger  # after editing API swagger comments
72	make help           # everything else
73	```
74
75	**Frontend only.** `pnpm install` then `pnpm exec vite build`; no Go rebuild needed for CSS or TS
76	changes if you are running `make watch`.
77
78	**The rebuild loop.** A `.go` change needs the binary rebuilt and restarted. A `.ts` or `.css`
79	change needs the frontend assets rebuilt. A `.tmpl` or locale change is picked up on reload in
80	development. `make watch` covers all of them (`docs/development.md`).
81
82	## Gotchas
83
84	- `make lint-go` is slow on a cold cache. Run it once before pushing rather than on every save.
85	- `make lint-templates` builds `.venv` by running `uv sync`, so without `uv` on `PATH` it fails with
86	  `make: uv: No such file or directory` — an error that never names the tool you are missing.
87	- `make fmt` can reformat files you never touched. Check `git status` afterwards and revert
88	  unrelated hunks, or they land in your commit.
89	- A swagger comment edit that is not followed by `make generate-swagger` passes locally and fails
90	  CI.
91	- Build artifacts (`gitea`, `data/`, `custom/`, `public/assets/*`) are gitignored — check
92	  `git status` before committing (`STUDENTS.md` §7).
93	- The repository expects LF endings; a CRLF commit shows as a whole-file diff.
94
95	## Related
96
97	- `testing.md` — the test targets
98	- `architecture.md` — what the layers are that you are linting
99
```

func TestAddDeletedBranch(t *testing.T) {
	assert.NoError(t, unittest.PrepareTestDatabase())
	repo := unittest.AssertExistsAndLoadBean(t, &repo_model.Repository{ID: 1})
	assert.Equal(t, git.Sha1ObjectFormat.Name(), repo.ObjectFormatName)
	firstBranch := unittest.AssertExistsAndLoadBean(t, &git_model.Branch{ID: 1})

	assert.True(t, firstBranch.IsDeleted)
	assert.NoError(t, git_model.MarkBranchAsDeleted(t.Context(), repo.ID, firstBranch.Name, firstBranch.DeletedByID))
	assert.NoError(t, git_model.MarkBranchAsDeleted(t.Context(), repo.ID, "branch2", int64(1)))

	secondBranch := unittest.AssertExistsAndLoadBean(t, &git_model.Branch{RepoID: repo.ID, Name: "branch2"})
	assert.True(t, secondBranch.IsDeleted)

	commit := &git.Commit{
		ID:            git.MustIDFromString(secondBranch.CommitID),
		CommitMessage: git.CommitMessage{MessageRaw: secondBranch.CommitMessage},
		Committer: &git.Signature{
			When: secondBranch.CommitTime.AsLocalTime(),
		},
	}

	_, err := git_model.UpdateBranch(t.Context(), repo.ID, secondBranch.PusherID, secondBranch.Name, commit)
	assert.NoError(t, err)
}

func TestGetDeletedBranches(t *testing.T) {
	assert.NoError(t, unittest.PrepareTestDatabase())
	repo := unittest.AssertExistsAndLoadBean(t, &repo_model.Repository{ID: 1})

	branches, err := db.Find[git_model.Branch](t.Context(), git_model.FindBranchOptions{
		ListOptions:     db.ListOptionsAll,
		RepoID:          repo.ID,
		IsDeletedBranch: optional.Some(true),
	})
	assert.NoError(t, err)
	assert.Len(t, branches, 2)
}

## 1. `templates/repo/branch/list.tmpl` (270 lines)

**Two separate renderings:** the default branch gets its own table (lines 16–76, using `.DefaultBranchBranch`), and the rest are in `{{range .Branches}}` (lines 91–211). A badge would need to be added in both places if you want it on the default branch too.

**Where "Updated X ago" / `CommitTime` is rendered** — the `<p class="info">` line, once per section:

- Default branch, line 30:
```gotemplate
<p class="info tw-flex tw-items-center tw-my-1">{{svg "octicon-git-commit" 16 "tw-mr-1"}}<a href="{{.RepoLink}}/commit/{{PathEscape .DefaultBranchBranch.DBBranch.CommitID}}">{{ShortSha .DefaultBranchBranch.DBBranch.CommitID}}</a> · <span class="commit-message">{{ctx.RenderUtils.RenderCommitMessage .DefaultBranchBranch.DBBranch.CommitMessage .Repository}}</span> · {{ctx.Locale.Tr "org.repo_updated"}} {{DateUtils.TimeSince .DefaultBranchBranch.DBBranch.CommitTime}}{{if .DefaultBranchBranch.DBBranch.Pusher}} ...{{end}}</p>
```
- Non-default branches, line 109 (same shape, `.DBBranch.CommitTime`, `$.Repository`).

**Where `IsDeleted` is checked** (note two different things named similarly):
- Line 94: `{{if .DBBranch.IsDeleted}}` — the per-branch model field; deleted branches render a plain `<span>` name + `repo.branch.deleted_by` info line (lines 95–99), `{{else}}` the live branch block (lines 100–109).
- Guards elsewhere: lines 113 (`{{if and (not .DBBranch.IsDeleted) $.DefaultBranchBranch}}`), 139, 145, 163, 176, 185, 196.
- Lines 9, 34, 56 use a bare root-scope `.IsDeleted` in the default-branch section. I grepped `routers/web/repo` and `services/context` and found **no `ctx.Data["IsDeleted"]` ever set** — so in `Branches()` this is always the zero value (falsy → `not .IsDeleted` is true). Pre-existing quirk; don't copy it.

**Where the default branch is identified:** purely by the separate `.DefaultBranchBranch` variable (lines 16, 113, 116, 118); there is no per-row `IsDefault` flag inside `{{range .Branches}}` — `LoadBranches` excludes the default branch from the list (see §3).

**Existing `ui label` badges** — the third `<td class="three wide tw-text-right">`, lines 133–160. This is the natural place for a "Stale" badge:
```gotemplate
{{if .IsIncluded}}
    <span class="ui orange large label" data-tooltip-content="{{ctx.Locale.Tr "repo.branch.included_desc"}}">
        {{svg "octicon-git-pull-request"}} {{ctx.Locale.Tr "repo.branch.included"}}
    </span>
...
    <a href="{{.LatestPullRequest.Issue.Link}}" class="ui purple large label">{{svg "octicon-git-merge" 16 "tw-mr-1"}}{{ctx.Locale.Tr "repo.pulls.merged"}}</a>
{{else if .LatestPullRequest.Issue.IsClosed}}
    <a href="{{.LatestPullRequest.Issue.Link}}" class="ui red large label">{{svg "octicon-git-pull-request-closed" 16 "tw-mr-1"}}{{ctx.Locale.Tr "repo.issues.closed_title"}}</a>
{{else}}
    <a href="{{.LatestPullRequest.Issue.Link}}" class="ui green large label">{{svg "octicon-git-pull-request" 16 "tw-mr-1"}}{{ctx.Locale.Tr "repo.issues.open_title"}}</a>
{{end}}
```
Caveat: that whole `<td>` is one if/else chain, so a Stale badge placed inside it would be mutually exclusive with the PR label. Placing it in the `flex-text-block` (next to the protected-branch shield, line 103–105) or at the end of the `<p class="info">` line avoids that.

Relevant locale keys live in `/workspaces/gitea/options/locale/locale_en-US.json` (JSON, not ini, in this tree): `"repo.branch.included"` line 2701, `"repo.branch.included_desc"` line 2700, `"org.repo_updated"` line 2743.

## 2. `models/git/branch.go` — the `Branch` struct

Lines 101–122:
```go
type Branch struct {
	ID            int64
	RepoID        int64                  `xorm:"UNIQUE(s)"`
	Repo          *repo_model.Repository `xorm:"-"`
	Name          string                 `xorm:"UNIQUE(s) NOT NULL"`
	CommitID      string
	CommitMessage string `xorm:"TEXT"` // it only stores the message summary (the first line)
	PusherID      int64
	Pusher        *user_model.User `xorm:"-"`
	IsDeleted     bool             `xorm:"index"`
	DeletedByID   int64
	DeletedBy     *user_model.User   `xorm:"-"`
	DeletedUnix   timeutil.TimeStamp `xorm:"index"`
	CommitTime    timeutil.TimeStamp // The commit
	CreatedUnix   timeutil.TimeStamp `xorm:"created"`
	UpdatedUnix   timeutil.TimeStamp `xorm:"updated"`
}
```
Methods on `*Branch` are only loaders — `LoadDeletedBy` (line 124), `LoadPusher` (135), `LoadRepo` (146). No time/staleness helper exists. `CommitTime` is a `timeutil.TimeStamp` (unix seconds); useful helpers in `/workspaces/gitea/modules/timeutil/timestamp.go`: `Add(seconds int64)` (43), `AddDuration` (48), `AsTime()` (58), `IsZero()` (99), and `timeutil.TimeStampNow()`.

Note: adding an `IsStale()` method directly on `models/git.Branch` would make `models/git` import `modules/setting`, which is acceptable in Gitea but the cleaner fit is a computed field on the service-layer view model (§3).

`/workspaces/gitea/routers/web/repo/branch.go`:
- `Branches(ctx)` at line 38, template const `tplBranch = "repo/branch/list"` (line 35).
- Line 56 fetches the data:

```
- Lines 84–88 set the template data: `ctx.Data["Branches"] = branches`, `ctx.Data["DefaultBranchBranch"] = defaultBranchOptional`, plus `CommitStatus`, `CommitStatuses`, `Keyword`, `Page`.

This is where an `IsStale bool` field belongs.

Default branch comes from `git_model.GetBranch(ctx, repo.ID, repo.DefaultBranch)` (line 63) and is **excluded** from the paged list via `ExcludeBranchNames: []string{repo.DefaultBranch}` (line 75); it is loaded separately at lines 111–116 and returned as the first return value.

Two variants exist. The `ini:"repository.x"` tag variant is what you want for `[repository.branch]`.

**Declaration** (inside the anonymous `Repository` struct), lines 105–115:
```go

			LockReasons []string

			MaxFiles         int64

```
`PullRequest` (lines 86–104) uses `ini:"repository.pull-request"` and contains e.g. `DelayCheckForInactiveDays int` — the closest analogue to `STALE_BRANCH_DAYS` (an int-days knob).

**Defaults** — repeat the full anonymous struct type in the composite literal, lines 248–265:
```go
		// Issue settings
		Issue: struct {
			LockReasons []string
			MaxPinned   int
		}{
			LockReasons: strings.Split("Too heated,Off-topic,Spam,Resolved", ","),
			MaxPinned:   3,
		},
```
(`PullRequest` defaults: lines 212–246, incl. `DelayCheckForInactiveDays: 7`.)

**Loading** — `loadRepositoryFrom` at line 298, mapping block lines 330–340:
```go
	if err = sec.MapTo(&Repository); err != nil {
		log.Fatal("Failed to map Repository settings: %v", err)
	} else if err = rootCfg.Section("repository.editor").MapTo(&Repository.Editor); err != nil {
		log.Fatal("Failed to map Repository.Editor settings: %v", err)
	} else if err = rootCfg.Section("repository.upload").MapTo(&Repository.Upload); err != nil {
		log.Fatal("Failed to map Repository.Upload settings: %v", err)
	} else if err = rootCfg.Section("repository.pull-request").MapTo(&Repository.PullRequest); err != nil {
		log.Fatal("Failed to map Repository.PullRequest settings: %v", err)
	}
```
Key distinction: `Editor` and `Upload` are tagged `ini:"-"` (lines 73–84) and **must** be mapped explicitly here; tagged sub-structs like `Issue`/`Release`/`Signing` are picked up automatically by `sec.MapTo(&Repository)` via the `ini:"repository.x"` tag. So `Branch struct { StaleBranchDays int } \`ini:"repository.branch"\`` needs only the declaration + default literal — no change to `loadRepositoryFrom`. Field-name→key derivation is go-ini's default (`StaleBranchDays` → `STALE_BRANCH_DAYS`); explicit overrides use tags like `CRUDActions []string \`ini:"CRUD_ACTIONS"\`` (line 123).

**Docs to update:** `/workspaces/gitea/custom/conf/app.example.ini` — sub-sections are documented as commented blocks, e.g. `;[repository.pull-request]` at line 1158, `;[repository.issue]` at 1213, `;[repository.release]` at 1223, with the `;DELAY_CHECK_FOR_INACTIVE_DAYS = 7` style at line 1206.

**Template access to settings:** templates don't reach `setting.Repository` directly; `/workspaces/gitea/modules/templates/helper.go` (lines ~76–126) exposes individual values as funcs. Since the staleness flag is best computed in `loadOneBranch`, no new template helper is needed.

I'm in read-only exploration mode, so nothing was modified. Here are the findings.

## 1. Locale file: format and the `repo.branch.*` block

**Format: flat JSON** (not ini). `/workspaces/gitea/options/locale/locale_en-US.json` is a single flat JSON object where "nesting" is expressed purely as **dot-separated key strings**, e.g. `"repo.branch.deleted_by"`. There is no `locale_en-US.ini` anymore. Keys are ordered by logical grouping (not alphabetically), so you insert new keys next to their siblings.

The `repo.branch.*` block lives at **lines 2676–2714** of `/workspaces/gitea/options/locale/locale_en-US.json`, sandwiched between `repo.release.*` (ends line 2675) and `repo.tag.*` (starts line 2715). The tail end of the block, where `stale` keys would naturally go (right after the `included`/divergence tooltips, which are the closest analogues):

```json
  "repo.branch.rename": "Rename Branch \"%s\"",
  "repo.branch.included_desc": "This branch is part of the default branch",
  "repo.branch.included": "Included",
  "repo.branch.create_new_branch": "Create branch from branch:",
  ...
  "repo.branch.commits_divergence_from": "Commit divergence: %[1]d behind and %[2]d ahead of %[3]s",
  "repo.branch.commits_no_divergence": "The same as branch %[1]s",
```

Naming conventions to follow:
- Badge label + its tooltip pair is `X` / `X_desc` (see `included` / `included_desc`), **not** `X_tooltip`. If you want to match house style, prefer `repo.branch.stale` + `repo.branch.stale_desc`; `stale_tooltip` would be a novel suffix in this file.
- Single-arg substitution uses bare `%s` (`"Deleted by %s"`, `"Rename Branch \"%s\""`).
- Multi-arg / reorderable substitution uses indexed verbs: `%[1]d`, `%[2]d`, `%[3]s`.
- Quotes inside values are escaped `\"`.
- The file is covered by spellcheck and editorconfig lint (`/workspaces/gitea/Makefile:143-144`), so keep 2-space indent and no trailing whitespace.

Existing "stale" strings elsewhere for wording precedent: `repo.issues.review.stale` = `"Updated since approval"`, `repo.settings.dismiss_stale_approvals`.

## 2. Tooltips in templates

Mechanism: a plain `data-tooltip-content="..."` attribute on any element; the value is the already-translated string. Examples:

Plain translated string — `/workspaces/gitea/templates/repo/branch/list.tmpl:27`:
```gotemplate
<span data-tooltip-content="{{ctx.Locale.Tr "repo.settings.protected_branch"}}">{{svg "octicon-shield-lock"}}</span>
```

With a parameter substituted — `/workspaces/gitea/templates/repo/branch/list.tmpl:167`:
```gotemplate
data-tooltip-content="{{ctx.Locale.Tr "repo.branch.new_branch_from" .DBBranch.Name}}"
```

With a parameter, multi-arg, precomputed into a variable — `/workspaces/gitea/templates/repo/branch/list.tmpl:133-139`. This is the closest pattern to what a `stale_tooltip` with a day count would want:
```gotemplate
{{$tooltipDivergence := ""}}
{{if or .CommitsBehind .CommitsAhead}}
    {{$tooltipDivergence = ctx.Locale.Tr "repo.branch.commits_divergence_from" .CommitsBehind .CommitsAhead $.DefaultBranchBranch.DBBranch.Name}}
{{else}}
    {{$tooltipDivergence = ctx.Locale.Tr "repo.branch.commits_no_divergence" $.DefaultBranchBranch.DBBranch.Name}}
{{end}}
<div class="commit-divergence" data-tooltip-content="{{$tooltipDivergence}}">
```

Other parameterized examples: `/workspaces/gitea/templates/repo/header.tmpl:42` (`ctx.Locale.Tr "repo.transfer.accept_desc" $.RepoTransfer.Recipient.GetDisplayName`) and `/workspaces/gitea/templates/repo/release/list.tmpl:90` (`ctx.Locale.Tr "repo.release.download_count" (ctx.Locale.PrettyNumber $att.DownloadCount)` — note the nested-call parenthesization you'd need for a formatted number of days).

## 4. Test patterns and where a stale test belongs

**`/workspaces/gitea/models/git/branch_test.go`** — package `git_test`, DB-backed. Every test starts with `assert.NoError(t, unittest.PrepareTestDatabase())` and uses `unittest.AssertExistsAndLoadBean(t, &repo_model.Repository{ID: 1})` plus `t.Context()`. This is heavyweight: it needs fixtures and `main_test.go` bootstrapping. Only appropriate if stale-ness becomes a DB query (e.g. a `FindBranchOptions` filter).

**`/workspaces/gitea/modules/setting/repository_test.go`** — package `setting` (internal), pure, no DB. This is the cleanest structure to copy for a "stale / not stale / disabled" matrix:
```go
func TestLoadRepositoryCreationLimits(t *testing.T) {
	defer test.MockVariableValue(&Repository.MaxCreationLimit)()
	t.Run("ShortcutPropagatesToBoth", func(t *testing.T) {
		cfg, err := NewConfigProviderFromData(`
[repository]
MAX_CREATION_LIMIT = 5
`)
		assert.NoError(t, err)
		loadRepositoryFrom(cfg)
		assert.Equal(t, 5, Repository.MaxCreationLimit)
	})
	...
}
```
Key idioms: `defer test.MockVariableValue(&Setting.Field)()` to restore globals, `NewConfigProviderFromData(ini string)`, call the unexported `loadXxxFrom(cfg)`, then `t.Run` subtests per case.

**Template-func tests do exist**, in package `templates`, calling the unexported funcs directly or through a mini `template.New("test")`:
- `/workspaces/gitea/modules/templates/helper_test.go` — `TestTemplateIif` builds `tmpl.Funcs(template.FuncMap{"Iif": iif})`, parses a snippet, executes into a `strings.Builder`, asserts output.
- `/workspaces/gitea/modules/templates/util_date_test.go` — `TestDateTime` uses `defer test.MockVariableValue(&setting.DefaultUILocation, testTz)()` and `timeutil.TimeStamp` reference times. This is the single best model for a stale test, since stale-ness is a timestamp-vs-threshold computation.
- `/workspaces/gitea/modules/templates/util_test.go`, `util_format_test.go`, `util_render_test.go` — table-driven `cases := []struct{...}` style.

**Recommendation:** if stale-ness is a pure function of `Branch.CommitTime` + a setting threshold, put the unit test in `/workspaces/gitea/modules/templates/` (mirroring `util_date_test.go`, with `test.MockVariableValue` for the threshold setting) or as a small method test next to wherever the predicate lives. A separate `modules/setting/*_test.go` case should cover only the config parsing (value set / value zero = disabled / default). The "renders the badge" end-to-end assertion belongs in `/workspaces/gitea/tests/integration/branches_test.go`, which already does exactly this shape:
```go
func TestViewBranches(t *testing.T) {
	defer tests.PrepareTestEnv(t)()
	req := NewRequest(t, "GET", "/user2/repo1/branches")
	resp := MakeRequest(t, req, http.StatusOK)
	htmlDoc := NewHTMLParser(t, resp.Body)
	AssertHTMLElement(t, htmlDoc, "[data-testid=branches-default-branch-list]", 1)
```
Note the `data-testid` convention already present in `list.tmpl` — a `data-testid=branch-stale-label` would fit.

There is **no** `services/repository/branch_test.go` — that package has `main_test.go` + others but nothing for branch.go, so you'd be creating a new file if you test `LoadBranches`.

## 5. Template func registration vs. computing in Go

Registration is a single map in `/workspaces/gitea/modules/templates/helper.go:26`, `func newFuncMapWebPage() template.FuncMap`, consumed at `/workspaces/gitea/modules/templates/page.go:28`. You'd add an entry like:
```go
"CountFmt": countFmt,
"Sec2Hour": util.SecToHours,
```
Note the comment in that file: *"it's lowercase because this name has been widely used. Our other functions should have uppercase names."* — new funcs get UpperCamelCase names. Settings-backed funcs are already a first-class pattern there, e.g.:
```go
"EnableTimetracking": func() bool {
    return setting.Service.EnableTimetracking
},
```
There is also a "utils object" pattern (`"DateUtils": NewDateUtils`, `"StringUtils": NewStringUtils`) for grouping related helpers.

**However, computing in Go is the better fit here.** The branch page already passes a purpose-built view struct — `/workspaces/gitea/services/repository/branch.go:51`:
```go
// Branch contains the branch information
type Branch struct {
	DBBranch          *git_model.Branch
	IsProtected       bool
	IsIncluded        bool
	CommitsAhead      int
	CommitsBehind     int
	LatestPullRequest *issues_model.PullRequest
	MergeMovedOn      bool
}
```
`IsProtected` / `IsIncluded` / `MergeMovedOn` are precedent for exactly this: a derived boolean computed in `loadOneBranch` and consumed as `{{if .IsIncluded}}` in the template. An `IsStale bool` field (populated in `loadOneBranch`, using `DBBranch.CommitTime` which is a `timeutil.TimeStamp` — `/workspaces/gitea/models/git/branch.go:119`) keeps the template dumb, is trivially unit-testable, and avoids adding a global template func for one page. The router that hands it to the template is `/workspaces/gitea/routers/web/repo/branch.go:86` (`ctx.Data["Branches"] = branches`), where you could also set `ctx.Data["StaleBranchThreshold"]` if the tooltip needs the day count.

// NewConfigProviderFromData this function is mainly for testing purpose
func NewConfigProviderFromData(configContent string) (ConfigProvider, error) {
	cfg, err := ini.LoadSources(configProviderLoadOptions(), strings.NewReader(configContent))
	if err != nil {
		return nil, err
	}
	cfg.NameMapper = ini.SnackCase
	return &iniConfigProvider{
		ini:             cfg,
		loadedFromEmpty: true,
	}, nil
}

		isExist, err := util.IsExist(file)
		if err != nil {
			return nil, fmt.Errorf("unable to check if %q exists: %v", file, err)
		}
		if isExist {
			if err = cfg.Append(file); err != nil {
				return nil, fmt.Errorf("failed to load config file %q: %v", file, err)
			}
			loadedFromEmpty = false
		}
	}

	cfg.NameMapper = ini.SnackCase
	return &iniConfigProvider{
		file:            file,
		ini:             cfg,
		loadedFromEmpty: loadedFromEmpty,
	}, nil
}
```

**Where should the Stale badge appear in the branch row?**

Options:
- **Next to branch name (Recommended)** - Inside the existing flex-text-block, after the protected-branch shield and commit statuses. Independent of the PR-label column, so it never competes with 'Included'/'Open'/'Merged' labels.
- **In the right-hand label column** - Beside the existing PR-status labels. Matches the issue's 'reuse the ui label style' note most literally, but that cell is one long if/else chain — the badge would be mutually exclusive with the PR label unless the chain is restructured.

**How much test coverage should this ship with?**

Options:
- **Unit + integration (Recommended)** - Pure unit test for Branch.IsStale (stale / fresh / disabled / deleted), a settings-parsing test, plus one assertion in tests/integration/branches_test.go that the badge renders on /user2/repo1/branches. Fixture branch2 has a 2020 commit time, so it is deterministic.
- **Unit tests only** - Just the two unit tests. Matches the issue's stated acceptance criterion ('a unit test covers the stale / not stale / disabled cases') and AGENTS.md's preference for unit over integration tests. The rendered badge itself would go unverified by CI.


**Answer:** Next to branch name (Recommended), Unit + integration (Recommended)
</details></tool-use>

# Show a "Stale" badge on branches with no recent commits (issue #11)

## Context

The branch list at `/{owner}/{repo}/branches` already renders "Updated 4 months ago" for every
row, but spotting abandoned branches means reading each row's date one by one. This adds a
visual-only **Stale** badge to branches whose latest commit is older than a configurable
threshold (default 90 days), so maintainers can find dead branches at a glance.

Note: branch `11-show-a-stale-badge-...` and the merged PR #31 reused this issue's branch name but
actually shipped the *deadline warning colour* work (issue #3). Nothing for issue #11 exists yet —
this is a clean start, and the current branch is identical to `main`.

No new DB columns and no new git calls: `Branch.CommitTime` is already persisted and already
rendered. The badge is purely presentational — it never deletes, blocks, or changes a branch.

## Approach

A pure predicate on the existing model (`Branch.IsStale()`), read directly by the template. The
default-branch and deleted-branch exclusions fall out of the template's existing structure rather
than needing extra conditions:

- `LoadBranches` sets `ExcludeBranchNames: []string{repo.DefaultBranch}`
  ([services/repository/branch.go:76](services/repository/branch.go#L76)), so the default branch is
  **never** in `.Branches`. It is rendered by a separate block from `.DefaultBranchBranch`
  ([list.tmpl:16-76](templates/repo/branch/list.tmpl#L16-L76)) which we simply do not touch.
- Deleted branches render inside `{{if .DBBranch.IsDeleted}}`
  ([list.tmpl:94-99](templates/repo/branch/list.tmpl#L94-L99)); the badge goes in the `{{else}}`
  block only. `IsStale()` also guards `IsDeleted` itself, so both layers agree.

This needs no change to `services/repository.Branch`.

## Changes

### 1. Setting — [modules/setting/repository.go](modules/setting/repository.go)

Add a tagged sub-struct next to the existing `Issue` / `Release` ones (~line 108):

```go
Branch struct {
	StaleBranchDays int
} `ini:"repository.branch"`
```

and its default in the composite literal next to `Issue:` (~line 249):

```go
Branch: struct {
	StaleBranchDays int
}{
	StaleBranchDays: 90,
},
```

**No change to `loadRepositoryFrom` is needed.** Verified: for a nested struct field go-ini
resolves the section by the `ini:` tag verbatim (`struct.go:322` → `SectionsByName(fieldName)`), so
`sec.MapTo(&Repository)` picks up `[repository.branch]` automatically — the same way `Issue`,
`Release` and `Signing` work. `cfg.NameMapper = ini.SnackCase`
([config_provider.go:197](modules/setting/config_provider.go#L197)) maps `StaleBranchDays` →
`STALE_BRANCH_DAYS`. The explicit `MapTo` calls at lines 332-338 exist only because `Editor` and
`Upload` are tagged `ini:"-"`.

Document it in [custom/conf/app.example.ini](custom/conf/app.example.ini) as a commented block
beside `;[repository.issue]` (line 1213), matching the `;MAX_PINNED = 3` style:

```ini
;[repository.branch]
;;
;; Branches whose latest commit is older than this many days are shown as stale. Set to 0 to disable.
;STALE_BRANCH_DAYS = 90
```

(There is no config cheat-sheet in this fork — `app.example.ini` is the only config doc.)

### 2. Model predicate — [models/git/branch.go](models/git/branch.go)

Add a method alongside the existing `LoadDeletedBy` / `LoadPusher` / `LoadRepo` methods (~line 152).
`models/git` already imports `modules/setting` in sibling files, so this introduces no new layer
dependency; add `"time"` and `"gitea.dev/modules/setting"` to this file's imports.

```go
// IsStale reports whether the branch has seen no commit within the configured window.
// A threshold of 0 or less turns the check off.
func (b *Branch) IsStale() bool {
	days := setting.Repository.Branch.StaleBranchDays
	if days <= 0 || b.IsDeleted || b.CommitTime.IsZero() {
		return false
	}
	return b.CommitTime < timeutil.TimeStampNow().AddDuration(-time.Duration(days)*24*time.Hour)
}
```

`timeutil.TimeStampNow()` and `TimeStamp.AddDuration` / `IsZero` already exist
([modules/timeutil/timestamp.go:35,48,99](modules/timeutil/timestamp.go#L35)).

### 3. Threshold for the tooltip — [routers/web/repo/branch.go](routers/web/repo/branch.go)

One line in `Branches()`, next to the other `ctx.Data` assignments (~line 85). `setting` is already
imported in this file.

```go
ctx.Data["StaleBranchDays"] = setting.Repository.Branch.StaleBranchDays
```

### 4. Badge markup — [templates/repo/branch/list.tmpl](templates/repo/branch/list.tmpl)

Inside the `{{else}}` (non-deleted) block, at the end of the `flex-text-block` div — i.e. after the
`repo/commit_statuses` include on [line 107](templates/repo/branch/list.tmpl#L107), before the
closing `</div>` on line 108:

```gotemplate
{{if .DBBranch.IsStale}}
	<span class="ui yellow label" data-testid="branch-stale-label" data-tooltip-content="{{ctx.Locale.Tr "repo.branch.stale_desc" $.StaleBranchDays}}">{{ctx.Locale.Tr "repo.branch.stale"}}</span>
{{end}}
```

Deliberately **not** in the `three wide tw-text-right` cell (lines 133-160): that cell is a single
if/else chain, so a badge there would be mutually exclusive with the Included/Open/Merged PR label.

`data-tooltip-content` with a translated, parameterised string is the established pattern here
(see [list.tmpl:167](templates/repo/branch/list.tmpl#L167)). `.tmpl` files are tab-indented.

### 5. Locale — [options/locale/locale_en-US.json](options/locale/locale_en-US.json)

Flat JSON with dotted keys, 2-space indent. Add next to `repo.branch.included` / `included_desc`
(~lines 2700-2701), following the house `X` / `X_desc` badge+tooltip convention (**not**
`_tooltip`):

```json
"repo.branch.stale": "Stale",
"repo.branch.stale_desc": "No commits in %d+ days",
```

Only `locale_en-US.json` is edited — every other locale comes from Crowdin.

## Tests

**Unit — `TestBranchIsStale` in [models/git/branch_test.go](models/git/branch_test.go)** (pure, no
DB, no `PrepareTestDatabase()`). Table-driven over a `git_model.Branch` built with `CommitTime`
relative to `timeutil.TimeStampNow()`, using
`defer test.MockVariableValue(&setting.Repository.Branch.StaleBranchDays, 90)()` — the pattern
already used in [models/git/lfs_test.go:32](models/git/lfs_test.go#L32). Cases:

| Case | Setup | Expect |
| --- | --- | --- |
| stale | commit 120 days ago, threshold 90 | `true` |
| not stale | commit 10 days ago, threshold 90 | `false` |
| boundary | commit 89 days ago, threshold 90 | `false` |
| disabled | commit 120 days ago, threshold 0 | `false` |
| deleted | commit 120 days ago, `IsDeleted: true` | `false` |
| zero commit time | `CommitTime: 0` | `false` |

**Unit — settings parsing in
[modules/setting/repository_test.go](modules/setting/repository_test.go)**, copying the
`TestLoadRepositoryCreationLimits` shape (`NewConfigProviderFromData` + `loadRepositoryFrom(cfg)` +
`t.Run` subtests, with `test.MockVariableValue` to restore the global): default is 90 when the
section is absent; `[repository.branch] STALE_BRANCH_DAYS = 30` yields 30; `= 0` yields 0. This
subtest is also what proves the tag-only ini mapping actually binds.

**Integration — [tests/integration/branches_test.go](tests/integration/branches_test.go)**, added to
the existing `TestViewBranches` shape (`defer tests.PrepareTestEnv(t)()`, GET
`/user2/repo1/branches`, `NewHTMLParser`, `AssertHTMLElement`). Deterministic against the fixtures
in `models/fixtures/branch.yml`: `branch2` has `commit_time: 1579166279` (Jan 2020) and is not
deleted → badge; `master` is the default branch and renders in the separate block → no badge;
`foo`/`bar` are deleted → no badge. Assert exactly one
`[data-testid=branch-stale-label]`, which covers three acceptance criteria at once.

## Verification

```sh
go test -run '^TestBranchIsStale$' ./models/git/
go test -run 'Repository' ./modules/setting/
go test -run '^TestViewBranches$' ./tests/integration/
make fmt && make lint-go && make lint-templates && make lint-editorconfig
```

Manual check (`make watch`, then `/user2/repo1/branches` on a dev instance): `branch2` shows the
badge, hovering it reads "No commits in 90+ days", `master` and the deleted rows show nothing.
Setting `STALE_BRANCH_DAYS = 0` in `app.ini` removes every badge; a large value like `100000` also
removes them.

`CONTRIBUTING.md` requires **before/after screenshots on any UI-changing PR** — capture the
branches page both ways. Commit with a Conventional Commit subject and an
`Assisted-by:` trailer, and only after explicit human approval.

func TestFindRecentlyPushedNewBranchesUsesPushTime(t *testing.T) {
	assert.NoError(t, unittest.PrepareTestDatabase())

	repo := unittest.AssertExistsAndLoadBean(t, &repo_model.Repository{ID: 10})
	doer := unittest.AssertExistsAndLoadBean(t, &user_model.User{ID: 12})
	branch := unittest.AssertExistsAndLoadBean(t, &git_model.Branch{RepoID: repo.ID, Name: "outdated-new-branch"})

	commitUnix := time.Now().Add(-3 * time.Hour).Unix()
	pushUnix := time.Now().Add(-30 * time.Minute).Unix()
	_, err := db.GetEngine(t.Context()).Exec(
		"UPDATE branch SET commit_time = ?, updated_unix = ? WHERE id = ?",
		commitUnix,
		pushUnix,
		branch.ID,
	)
	assert.NoError(t, err)

	branches, err := git_model.FindRecentlyPushedNewBranches(t.Context(), doer, git_model.FindRecentlyPushedNewBranchesOptions{
		Repo:            repo,
		BaseRepo:        repo,
		PushedAfterUnix: time.Now().Add(-time.Hour).Unix(),
		MaxCount:        1,
	})
	assert.NoError(t, err)
	if assert.Len(t, branches, 1) {
		assert.Equal(t, branch.Name, branches[0].BranchName)
		assert.Equal(t, timeutil.TimeStamp(pushUnix), branches[0].PushedTime)

```text
// Copyright 2017 The Gitea Authors. All rights reserved.
// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT

package integration

import (
	"io"
	"testing"

	"gitea.dev/modules/test"

	"github.com/PuerkitoBio/goquery"
	"github.com/stretchr/testify/assert"
)

// HTMLDoc struct
type HTMLDoc struct {
	doc *goquery.Document
}

// NewHTMLParser parse html file
func NewHTMLParser(t testing.TB, body io.Reader) *HTMLDoc {
	t.Helper()
	doc, err := goquery.NewDocumentFromReader(body)
	assert.NoError(t, err)
	return &HTMLDoc{doc: doc}
}

// GetInputValueByName for get input value by name
func (doc *HTMLDoc) GetInputValueByName(name string) string {
	text, _ := doc.doc.Find(`input[name="` + name + `"]`).Attr("value")
	return text
}

// Find gets the descendants of each element in the current set of
// matched elements, filtered by a selector. It returns a new Selection
// object containing these matched elements.
func (doc *HTMLDoc) Find(selector string) *goquery.Selection {
	return doc.doc.Find(selector)
}

// AssertHTMLElement check if the element by selector exists or does not exist depending on checkExists
func AssertHTMLElement[T int | bool](t testing.TB, doc *HTMLDoc, selector string, checkExists T) {
	t.Helper()
	sel := doc.doc.Find(selector)
	switch v := any(checkExists).(type) {
	case bool:
		assert.Equal(t, v, sel.Length() > 0)
	case int:
		assert.Equal(t, v, sel.Length())
	}
}

func assertHTMLEq(t testing.TB, expected, actual string) {
	t.Helper()
	if expected == actual { // fast path
		return
	}
	exp := test.NormalizeHTMLAttributes(t, expected)
	act := test.NormalizeHTMLAttributes(t, actual)
	assert.Equal(t, exp, act)
}

+// IsStale reports whether the branch has seen no commit within the configured window.
+// A threshold of 0 or less turns the check off.
+func (b *Branch) IsStale() bool {
+	days := setting.Repository.Branch.StaleBranchDays
+	if days <= 0 || b.IsDeleted || b.CommitTime.IsZero() {
+		return false
+	}
+	return b.CommitTime < timeutil.TimeStampNow().AddDuration(-time.Duration(days)*24*time.Hour)

_**Agent (claude-sonnet-5 2026-09-16 21:23:25Z)**_

Implementation complete. Summary of changes for issue #11 (Stale branch badge):

**Backend**
- [modules/setting/repository.go](modules/setting/repository.go) — new `[repository.branch] STALE_BRANCH_DAYS` setting, default 90, following the existing `Issue`/`Release` sub-section pattern (no loader changes needed — verified go-ini binds the tagged section automatically).
- [models/git/branch.go](models/git/branch.go) — `Branch.IsStale()` predicate: false when disabled (`days <= 0`), deleted, or the commit time is zero/within the window.
- [routers/web/repo/branch.go](routers/web/repo/branch.go) — passes `StaleBranchDays` to the template for the tooltip text.
- [custom/conf/app.example.ini](custom/conf/app.example.ini) — documented the new option.
